evidence_items.publisher: ACM; abstract reproduced by the University of Vienna
evidence_items.locator: Abstract, sentence following the learning-gain result
evidence_items.explanation: The abstract reports significant learning gains even in the condition where every feedback instance contained errors, alongside lower perceived accuracy. This challenges a broad impossibility claim, but the accessible record does not establish that learners were uncertain which guidance to believe rather than able to identify and correct errors.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; Tomohiro Nagashima, Mirella Hladký and Vera Rief
evidence_items.explanation: The fall 2025 experiment warned some students that the tutor could make mistakes while keeping its actual feedback identical and error-free. It measured interaction and immediate performance, but explicitly omitted pre-test and post-test results, leaving the learning question unsettled.

unresolved_gaps: The retrieved evidence does not jointly establish uncertainty about believing the tutor and meaningful learning attributable to that tutor.
The fallibility-warning experiment does not report learning gains or directly verify the proposed psychological mechanism.
The full methods of the erroneous-feedback study were inaccessible through read_page.
